title: Project discovery
purpose: Build an evidence-backed application profile and architecture map before any specialized audit begins.
applies: A changed monorepo layout or deployment model
notApplies: A report-only replay with an unchanged, still-valid profile
checks: Detect languages, frameworks, package managers, applications, data stores, queues, providers, tests, CI, and deployment files
Map public, private, admin, tenant, upload, payment, and AI boundaries with file evidence
Record a confidence level and evidence list for every detected capability
manual: Confirm ambiguous service boundaries and critical user workflows
Compare detected deployment topology with operator documentation
safeFixes: Create missing local .forge report directories
Normalize a stale generated profile after discovery
approval: Changing application boundaries or deployment topology
Enabling a provider inferred only from dormant code
verify: Validate project-profile.json against its schema
Trace every architecture-map node back to profile evidence
stack: Prefer native workspace commands and manifest semantics for the detected package manager
limitations: Runtime-only infrastructure may remain NOT_VERIFIED without operator access

title: Requirements and domain logic
purpose: Trace business rules and acceptance criteria to executable behavior, including adverse and recovery paths.
notApplies: Pure formatting changes with no behavior impact
checks: Trace stated outcomes, invariants, duplicate-operation behavior, recovery, ownership, and offline assumptions to code and tests
Identify contradictory rules and hidden defaults at trust boundaries
Exercise success, empty, error, retry, cancellation, and partial-failure paths
manual: Confirm ambiguous business policy with an accountable owner
Review financial, entitlement, and lifecycle rules with representative examples
safeFixes: Add missing assertions for an already-established rule
Document an observed invariant and its evidence
approval: Changing business policy, ownership, pricing, or entitlement semantics
verify: Run targeted acceptance tests
Map every claimed requirement to code, test, or NOT_VERIFIED evidence
stack: Locate validation in the actual domain boundary rather than only the UI
limitations: Unwritten policy cannot be inferred as verified intent

title: Architecture
purpose: Evaluate system boundaries, dependency direction, failure domains, and the fitness of the current topology.
notApplies: A single isolated script with no service or data boundary
checks: Trace one critical request end to end across UI, API, jobs, data, and integrations
Detect cycles, boundary leakage, shared mutable state, and single points of failure
Compare complexity and operational cost with demonstrated requirements
manual: Validate context boundaries and ownership with maintainers
Review unavailable runtime dependencies and organization constraints
safeFixes: Add or update an architecture decision record
Clarify module ownership and dependency rules
approval: Splitting services, changing data ownership, or replacing core infrastructure
verify: Re-run dependency and boundary checks
Exercise the traced critical flow after structural changes
stack: Respect framework composition boundaries before introducing custom layers
limitations: Production traffic shape and organizational coupling require external evidence

title: Code quality
purpose: Find correctness, maintainability, type-safety, error-handling, and dead-code risks in changed and critical paths.
notApplies: Repositories containing only non-executable documentation
checks: Run available format, lint, type, unit, and build checks without hiding failures
Inspect boundary validation, error propagation, resource cleanup, concurrency, and unsafe casts
Compare changes with the newest established local precedent and remove only proven dead code
manual: Review complex control flow and public API clarity
Inspect generated or excluded paths not covered by tools
safeFixes: Apply deterministic formatting
Correct proven lint, typing, cleanup, and assertion defects
approval: Changing a public contract or broad behavior during cleanup
verify: Run gates after the final edit
Exercise the affected behavior rather than relying only on compilation
stack: Use the repository's pinned toolchain and scripts
limitations: Static analysis cannot prove runtime behavior or requirement intent

title: User interface
purpose: Inspect rendered interfaces for responsive behavior, hierarchy, state clarity, consistency, and visual defects.
notApplies: Headless services with no operator or user interface
checks: Inspect the running application at representative small, medium, and wide viewports where possible
Verify loading, empty, error, success, disabled, focus, hover, and long-content states
Check semantic tokens, typography hierarchy, spacing rhythm, image dimensions, overflow, and reduced motion
manual: Compare critical screens across themes and input methods
Judge visual hierarchy and brand consistency from captured evidence
safeFixes: Add missing accessible labels or non-breaking responsive constraints
Correct token use and layout-shift-causing dimensions
approval: Changing the product's visual language or interaction model
verify: Reinspect changed screens at 320, 375, 768, 1024, and 1440 CSS pixels
Confirm keyboard focus and no unintended horizontal overflow
stack: Use native framework semantics and preserve server/client rendering boundaries
limitations: Do not claim browser or device inspection unless it actually ran

title: User experience
purpose: Evaluate real task flows for clarity, feedback, recovery, accessibility, and avoidance of user harm.
applies: Onboarding, forms, search, checkout, or destructive flows
notApplies: Libraries with no end-user workflow
checks: Walk primary and adverse journeys from entry to durable outcome
Inspect labels, defaults, validation timing, progress, cancellation, retry, undo, and destructive confirmations
Verify that errors state cause and recovery and preserve user-entered data
manual: Assess information scent and cognitive load with realistic data
Review sensitive consent and irreversible actions for user control
safeFixes: Clarify labels, helper text, and error recovery
Add missing non-destructive feedback states
approval: Changing workflow order, consent, or destructive-action semantics
verify: Repeat representative journeys with keyboard and narrow viewport
Confirm durable state after refresh, retry, and duplicate action
stack: Test client and server transitions, including optimistic rollback
limitations: Usability conclusions without user research are hypotheses, not verified user outcomes

title: Accessibility
purpose: Audit conformance with WCAG 2.2 AA using automated evidence plus keyboard and assistive-technology reasoning.
notApplies: A protocol-only library with no human-facing output
checks: Check names, roles, states, landmarks, headings, labels, alternatives, contrast, zoom, reflow, target size, and status messages
Complete all critical workflows using keyboard only
Inspect focus order, focus trapping, restoration, errors, dynamic updates, and reduced motion
manual: Review accessible names in context and screen-reader reading order
Test high-risk custom widgets against the APG pattern
safeFixes: Associate labels, restore visible focus, and add missing semantic state
Add text alternatives supported by surrounding context
approval: Replacing a custom interaction or materially changing content meaning
verify: Re-run automated checks and keyboard walkthroughs
Map findings to exact WCAG success criteria
stack: Prefer native HTML or platform controls before ARIA-based reimplementation
limitations: Automated scanners cover only part of WCAG; unperformed assistive-technology tests are NOT_VERIFIED

title: Internationalization
purpose: Find locale, translation, formatting, expansion, fallback, and bidirectional-layout defects.
applies: Products handling names, addresses, dates, currency, or pluralization
notApplies: Locale-neutral internal protocols
checks: Detect user-facing hard-coded text and inconsistent translation keys
Inspect locale negotiation, fallback, pluralization, date, number, currency, time-zone, and collation behavior
Check text expansion, RTL direction, mirrored layout, Unicode input, and localized metadata
manual: Review culturally sensitive copy and incomplete translations
Exercise representative RTL and long-string layouts
safeFixes: Replace ad hoc formatting with existing locale utilities
Add missing fallback keys when translation intent is known
approval: Changing source copy, locale support policy, or financial formatting rules
verify: Run catalog consistency checks
Render representative locales and confirm fallback behavior
stack: Use the detected framework's routing and message extraction conventions
limitations: Translation quality requires qualified human review

title: Search discoverability
purpose: Conditionally inspect public web content for crawlability, canonicalization, metadata, structured data, and rendering.
applies: Marketing, documentation, catalog, or editorial content
notApplies: Private applications and routes intentionally excluded from search
checks: Verify status codes, indexability, canonical URLs, robots directives, sitemap coverage, titles, descriptions, and social metadata
Inspect server-rendered content, internal links, pagination, redirects, duplicate URLs, and structured-data validity
Separate performance evidence from unmeasured assumptions
manual: Judge search intent and snippet quality
Confirm private or tenant data is never made indexable
safeFixes: Correct deterministic canonical, robots, or metadata omissions
Add missing image dimensions and link descriptions
approval: Changing URL structure, redirect policy, or indexability
verify: Fetch representative routes as a crawler
Validate sitemap and structured data with recorded output
stack: Inspect both framework metadata APIs and final response HTML
limitations: Rankings and external index state cannot be promised from repository evidence

title: Frontend engineering
purpose: Inspect rendering, state, network, hydration, browser security, and bundle behavior in frontend applications.
notApplies: Backend-only services
checks: Trace data fetching, caching, cancellation, race handling, optimistic rollback, and stale-state behavior
Inspect rendering boundaries, hydration, error boundaries, code splitting, source maps, and browser compatibility
Check untrusted HTML, client secrets, CSRF assumptions, and sensitive storage
manual: Exercise slow, offline, duplicate, and out-of-order responses
Inspect bundle composition and runtime console output when tooling is available
safeFixes: Add abort handling, explicit states, and deterministic lazy boundaries
Remove confirmed client-side secret exposure
approval: Replacing state architecture or changing rendering strategy
verify: Run production build and representative browser flows
Confirm server/client output and network failure recovery
stack: Follow the detected framework's current server/client and cache semantics
limitations: Bundle and performance claims require measured artifacts

title: API design and implementation
purpose: Audit API contracts, boundary validation, authorization, consistency, pagination, errors, and idempotency.
applies: HTTP, GraphQL, RPC, or event-consumed application interfaces
notApplies: Applications with no machine-consumed interface
checks: Compare implemented routes, methods, schemas, status codes, errors, and versioning with the contract
Inspect input limits, mass assignment, object authorization, rate limits, pagination, filtering, and response data exposure
Verify idempotency and concurrency behavior for retryable or money-moving operations
manual: Review compatibility and deprecation policy
Inspect representative requests across roles and ownership boundaries
safeFixes: Add schema validation, explicit limits, and consistent error envelopes
Correct documentation that is demonstrably stale
approval: Changing a public contract, version, or authorization semantics
verify: Run contract and negative-boundary tests
Replay duplicates and unauthorized object identifiers
stack: Inspect the final router and middleware composition, not annotations alone
limitations: External consumer behavior requires compatibility evidence

title: Background jobs
purpose: Inspect queued and scheduled work for durability, idempotency, retries, poison messages, and operability.
applies: Queues, workers, cron, scheduled functions, and outbox consumers
notApplies: Applications with no asynchronous or scheduled execution
checks: Trace enqueue-to-effect flow and delivery guarantees
Inspect idempotency keys, leases, timeouts, retries, jitter, dead-letter handling, ordering, concurrency, and payload versioning
Verify transaction boundaries, outbox/inbox behavior, observability, replay, and shutdown
manual: Review operational replay and poison-message runbooks
Confirm provider retention and retry settings outside the repository
safeFixes: Add bounded retry metadata, structured job logging, and payload validation
Add tests for duplicate delivery
approval: Introducing a queue or changing delivery and ordering semantics
verify: Deliver the same job twice and observe one durable outcome
Force failure through retry and dead-letter paths
stack: Use provider-native acknowledgement and visibility-timeout semantics
limitations: Managed queue policy is NOT_VERIFIED without configuration output

title: External integrations
purpose: Audit outbound and inbound integrations for authentication, validation, failure isolation, drift, and replay safety.
applies: Third-party APIs, webhooks, SDKs, and service-to-service calls
notApplies: Self-contained applications with no external dependency
checks: Inspect timeouts, bounded retries, jitter, circuit behavior, rate limits, and fallback
Verify webhook signatures against raw bytes, freshness, replay defense, and event idempotency
Check credential scope, version pinning, data minimization, sandbox separation, and error redaction
manual: Review provider dashboards, quotas, and deprecation notices
Confirm contractual retention and incident obligations
safeFixes: Add explicit timeouts, payload validation, and secret redaction
Pin a compatible SDK version after tests
approval: Changing provider, credentials, contractual data flow, or failure policy
verify: Replay signed and tampered payloads
Simulate timeout, rate limit, and provider error responses
stack: Prefer official SDK verification primitives while validating their configured options
limitations: Provider-side state and contracts require external evidence

title: Authentication
purpose: Inspect identity proofing, credentials, sessions, recovery, federation, and reauthentication controls.
applies: Applications identifying users, services, or administrators
notApplies: Truly anonymous static content with no privileged operation
checks: Trace sign-up, sign-in, logout, recovery, verification, MFA, reauthentication, and account linking
Inspect password hashing, session rotation, expiry, cookie flags, CSRF, token audience/issuer/algorithm, enumeration, and brute-force defenses
Verify state-changing endpoints derive identity from trusted server context
manual: Review provider tenant settings and recovery support procedures
Test session revocation and high-risk reauthentication
safeFixes: Harden cookie flags and redact authentication errors
Add missing token claim validation supported by current configuration
approval: Replacing authentication, changing identity linkage, or rotating credentials
verify: Run positive and negative flows with expired, replayed, tampered, and cross-environment credentials
Confirm logout and revocation invalidate durable sessions
stack: Validate framework middleware order and provider defaults explicitly
limitations: Hosted-provider settings remain NOT_VERIFIED without exported configuration

title: Authorization
purpose: Verify deny-by-default function, object, role, tenant, and administrative authorization on every path.
applies: Any private, role-gated, owned, tenant, or administrative resource
notApplies: Public read-only content with no hidden data or action
checks: Build a subject-action-resource-context matrix for critical resources
Trace enforcement at server boundaries, jobs, exports, uploads, websockets, and indirect identifiers
Test horizontal, vertical, tenant, stale-role, bulk, and confused-deputy cases
manual: Confirm intended role semantics and ownership transitions
Review break-glass and support impersonation controls
safeFixes: Centralize an existing repeated policy check without semantic change
Add negative authorization tests
approval: Changing roles, policy semantics, tenant isolation, or administrative access
verify: Run the matrix with allowed and denied principals
Verify denied attempts are safely logged without sensitive data
stack: Never rely on UI visibility as authorization; test final data access
limitations: Policy intent requires an authoritative owner

title: Application security
purpose: Perform a threat-informed audit of trust boundaries, injection, secrets, browser controls, dependencies, and abuse cases.
notApplies: No exemption; scope may be reduced for non-executable documentation
checks: Model assets, actors, entry points, trust boundaries, abuse cases, and mitigations
Inspect injection, XSS, CSRF, SSRF, deserialization, path handling, redirects, headers, CORS, secrets, logging, and denial-of-service limits
Run available dependency, static, and secret checks while distinguishing confirmed evidence from pattern matches
manual: Review business-logic abuse and chained attack paths
Validate production-only controls with operators
safeFixes: Parameterize known trust-boundary inputs, redact secrets, and add straightforward security headers
Add allowlists and explicit size limits
approval: Disabling controls, rotating secrets, or changing authentication, network, or production infrastructure
verify: Re-run scanners and targeted exploit regression tests
Confirm every PASS has direct evidence
stack: Use framework-native escaping and query parameterization at the final sink
limitations: This audit is not a penetration test and must not be represented as one

title: Privacy
purpose: Inspect personal-data inventory, purpose, minimization, consent, retention, access, deletion, export, and logging.
applies: Applications processing personal, device, behavioral, or sensitive data
notApplies: Systems proven to process no data linkable to a person
checks: Map collection, purpose, legal basis or consent, storage, processors, transfer, retention, and deletion
Inspect logs, analytics, backups, exports, support access, subject requests, and privacy defaults
Verify sensitive fields are minimized, protected, and excluded from accidental telemetry
manual: Obtain qualified legal review for jurisdiction-specific obligations
Confirm processor contracts and production retention settings
safeFixes: Redact unnecessary personal data from logs
Document a verified data-flow or retention control
approval: Changing consent, retention, deletion, data sharing, or legal representations
verify: Trace representative data through create, access, export, deletion, and backup handling
Confirm telemetry does not receive prohibited fields
standards: OWASP User Privacy Protection Cheat Sheet
stack: Inspect generated telemetry and managed-service defaults, not schemas alone
limitations: Do not provide legal conclusions; mark missing policy evidence NOT_VERIFIED

title: Multi-tenancy
purpose: Verify tenant context propagation and isolation across data, cache, files, jobs, search, analytics, and administration.
applies: Shared applications serving distinct organizations or customer partitions
notApplies: Single-tenant deployments with no shared data plane
inputs: queries, cache keys, storage paths, and jobs
checks: Identify the trusted tenant-context source and follow it through every boundary
Test missing, forged, stale, and cross-tenant identifiers in reads, writes, bulk actions, exports, jobs, and websockets
Inspect composite uniqueness, row policies, cache namespaces, object prefixes, logs, and support tooling
manual: Review provisioning, suspension, migration, deletion, and break-glass flows
Validate database and provider isolation settings
safeFixes: Add tenant-scoped tests and explicit cache-key namespaces
Reject missing tenant context at an existing boundary
approval: Changing tenant identifiers, isolation strategy, or support access
verify: Run cross-tenant negative tests for every critical resource
Confirm asynchronous work restores trusted tenant context
standards: OWASP Multi Tenant Security Cheat Sheet
stack: Ensure ORM helpers cannot be bypassed by raw queries or background workers
limitations: Infrastructure-level isolation requires live configuration evidence

title: File uploads
purpose: Audit the complete upload, processing, storage, delivery, and deletion pipeline against hostile files.
applies: Imports, attachments, avatars, media, and generated files
notApplies: Systems with no file ingestion or user-controlled object references
checks: Trace authorization, filename normalization, extension and MIME allowlists, signature detection, size and count limits
Inspect archive bombs, path traversal, parser isolation, malware scanning, image re-encoding, metadata stripping, and quarantine
Verify private storage, random object names, signed URL scope/expiry, download headers, tenant boundaries, cleanup, and orphan handling
manual: Review provider bucket policy and malware-scanner failure mode
Exercise polyglot, oversized, malformed, duplicate, and unauthorized objects
safeFixes: Add explicit size/count limits and safe content-disposition
Normalize generated object names and log redaction
approval: Changing bucket visibility, accepted types, retention, or processing architecture
verify: Run a hostile-file fixture suite through the real pipeline
Confirm rejected and quarantined files are neither served nor orphaned
stack: Do not trust client MIME or original filenames; validate after streaming limits
limitations: Scanner effectiveness and storage policy need direct service evidence

title: Database design
purpose: Inspect schema integrity, migrations, constraints, tenancy, lifecycle, recovery, and production-safe evolution.
applies: Applications with a database or durable structured store
notApplies: Stateless applications proven to store no durable data
checks: Inspect keys, types, nullability, defaults, foreign keys, uniqueness, checks, indexes, and cascade behavior
Review migration ordering, transactional safety, locks, backfills, expand-contract compatibility, and rollback or forward-fix strategy
Trace tenant isolation, encryption, retention, audit fields, soft deletion, and backup expectations
manual: Review applied production migration state and large-table risk with operators
Confirm restore objectives and managed-database settings
safeFixes: Add documentation and tests for existing constraints
Create a new unapplied safe migration when lock and compatibility risk is understood
approval: Editing applied migrations, dropping data, changing ownership, or rewriting architecture
verify: Apply migrations to an empty and representative upgraded database
Run integrity and rollback/forward-fix tests
stack: Inspect generated SQL and actual constraints, not ORM declarations alone
limitations: Production row counts, locks, and plans cannot be inferred

title: Query behavior
purpose: Find correctness, injection, overfetching, N+1, pagination, locking, and index-use risks in data access.
applies: Database, search, analytics, and remote query code
notApplies: Systems with no queryable data source
checks: Trace user-controlled values to parameterized query boundaries
Detect N+1 patterns, unbounded reads, offset drift, incorrect joins, overfetching, missing ordering, and unsafe dynamic identifiers
Review transactions, isolation, locks, timeouts, connection use, batching, and candidate indexes
manual: Review real EXPLAIN output for high-impact queries
Confirm data-distribution and concurrency assumptions
safeFixes: Parameterize values, add explicit bounds, and select required columns
Add a proven non-disruptive index through a new migration
approval: Changing result semantics, isolation, production indexes, or query architecture
verify: Run correctness tests with boundary and concurrent cases
Compare measured plans before and after performance changes
stack: Account for ORM lazy loading, implicit transactions, and generated SQL
limitations: Never fabricate a query plan or production cardinality

title: Caching
purpose: First decide whether caching is justified, then audit keys, invalidation, consistency, privacy, and failure behavior.
applies: Detected caches, CDNs, memoization, or a measured proposal to add caching
notApplies: No cache and no measured latency or load need
checks: Require a measured bottleneck and explicit freshness contract before recommending a cache
Inspect key completeness, tenant and user scope, TTL, invalidation, stampede control, negative caching, serialization, and versioning
Check sensitive-data exposure, authorization changes, eviction, memory limits, outage fallback, and observability
manual: Review consistency tolerance with product owners
Validate managed cache eviction and network policy
safeFixes: Namespace incomplete keys and add bounded TTLs where semantics are established
Add cache hit/miss and fallback telemetry without sensitive values
approval: Introducing Redis or changing consistency and invalidation semantics
verify: Exercise hit, miss, stale, invalidated, stampede, and cache-down paths
Confirm cross-user and cross-tenant isolation
stack: Account for framework, CDN, browser, server, and data caches as separate layers
limitations: Cache value requires workload measurements

title: Object and file storage
purpose: Inspect object naming, access control, encryption, lifecycle, consistency, integrity, and recovery.
applies: Object stores, file systems, blob databases, and CDN-backed assets
notApplies: No persistent files or objects
checks: Trace create, read, replace, copy, list, and delete authorization
Inspect private-by-default policy, object naming, tenant prefixes, signed URL constraints, encryption, checksums, versioning, and lifecycle
Check orphan cleanup, partial writes, metadata leakage, CDN caching, legal holds, and restore expectations
manual: Review actual bucket, key, network, replication, and lifecycle policy
Test provider consistency and failure assumptions
safeFixes: Add integrity validation and explicit content headers
Add cleanup for proven temporary-object leaks
approval: Changing visibility, retention, replication, or deleting objects
verify: Exercise unauthorized and cross-tenant object access
Verify lifecycle and restore behavior with recorded provider output
stack: Treat presigned URLs as scoped credentials and bind method, object, size, and expiry
limitations: Repository configuration does not prove deployed bucket policy

title: Testing strategy
purpose: Evaluate whether tests provide reliable risk-based evidence across units, boundaries, workflows, and failure modes.
notApplies: Non-executable documentation-only packages
checks: Map critical risks to unit, integration, contract, end-to-end, migration, security, and accessibility tests
Inspect determinism, isolation, data factories, assertions, cleanup, time control, concurrency, and flaky retries
Verify tests can fail for the defect they claim to detect and do not overmock the boundary under test
manual: Review omitted high-impact scenarios and test maintainability
Inspect CI artifacts and quarantine policy
safeFixes: Add missing assertions and deterministic setup
Remove an unnecessary retry only after proving the test is stable
approval: Deleting coverage, weakening assertions, or changing product behavior to satisfy tests
verify: Run targeted tests before and after inducing a representative failure
Run the relevant full suite after final edits
stack: Use native test isolation and real boundary substitutes such as ephemeral databases where practical
limitations: Coverage percentage alone does not establish behavior coverage

title: Performance
purpose: Measure and improve user- and system-visible latency, throughput, resource use, and stability without guessing.
notApplies: No claimed or measured performance requirement
checks: Define representative workloads, devices, networks, data sizes, and percentile budgets
Measure frontend Core Web Vitals, bundle cost, server latency, database time, memory, CPU, I/O, and external calls as applicable
Identify the dominant bottleneck before changing code and check cold starts, concurrency, leaks, and backpressure
manual: Validate workload realism and user impact
Review production traces when authorized
safeFixes: Remove proven duplicate work and add bounded pagination
Declare dimensions and lazy-load noncritical assets after measurement
approval: Adding infrastructure, caches, denormalization, or behavior-changing approximations
verify: Repeat the same benchmark with uncertainty and environment recorded
Confirm correctness and tail latency did not regress
stack: Use production builds and framework profilers, never development timing as release proof
limitations: Do not invent performance measurements or extrapolate from unrelated hardware

title: Scalability
purpose: Assess growth limits, contention, partitioning, quotas, backpressure, and cost against explicit demand scenarios.
applies: Expected growth, load concentration, or capacity incidents
notApplies: No scale requirement beyond measured current capacity
checks: Model request, data, tenant, connection, queue, storage, and third-party growth
Find serial bottlenecks, hot keys, fan-out, unbounded work, connection exhaustion, and noisy neighbors
Inspect horizontal state, partition keys, rate shaping, load shedding, autoscaling signals, and graceful degradation
manual: Validate growth and burst assumptions with operators and product owners
Review regional and provider quota constraints
safeFixes: Add explicit bounds, batching, backpressure, and capacity telemetry
Document measured limits
approval: Introducing services, sharding, queues, caches, or multi-region topology
verify: Run staged load tests through saturation and recovery
Confirm correctness and tenant fairness under contention
stack: Account for framework connection pools, runtime concurrency, and managed-service quotas
limitations: Capacity projections are only as credible as workload evidence

title: Observability
purpose: Verify that logs, metrics, traces, events, alerts, and dashboards answer concrete operational questions safely.
notApplies: Pure build-time artifacts with no runtime behavior
checks: Trace a request across service, job, database, and integration boundaries with stable correlation
Inspect structured event names, metric units, cardinality, sampling, error status, service metadata, and deployment version
Check alert symptom quality, ownership, runbook links, SLO coverage, redaction, access, and retention
manual: Use telemetry to answer latency, error, saturation, and affected-user questions
Review deployed dashboards and paging routes
safeFixes: Add bounded context and correlation identifiers
Redact secrets and high-cardinality or personal fields
approval: Changing telemetry vendors, retention, sampling, or personal-data collection
verify: Generate a known success and failure and locate both in telemetry
Validate alerts with a controlled signal where safe
stack: Instrument framework and provider boundaries without double-counting spans
limitations: Instrumentation code does not prove deployed ingestion or alert delivery

title: Reliability
purpose: Audit timeouts, retries, overload, dependencies, degradation, consistency, and operational objectives.
applies: Services and critical workflows with availability or durability expectations
notApplies: Disposable local-only utilities with no reliability objective
checks: Define user-visible service indicators and error-budget expectations
Inspect timeout budgets, bounded retries, jitter, circuit behavior, health checks, overload, bulkheads, and dependency fallbacks
Check graceful shutdown, deploy overlap, consistency, partial failure, idempotency, and clock assumptions
manual: Review known failure modes and incident learnings
Confirm provider SLAs and operator escalation paths
safeFixes: Add bounded timeouts, retry classification, and graceful shutdown
Add health checks that reflect readiness without exposing internals
approval: Changing consistency, fail-open behavior, provider topology, or availability targets
verify: Inject dependency, timeout, overload, and shutdown failures
Confirm recovery without duplicate durable effects
stack: Align platform health and termination semantics with application lifecycle
limitations: Availability claims require measured production evidence

title: Backup and recovery
purpose: Verify recoverability of data and service against explicit RPO, RTO, corruption, deletion, and regional scenarios.
applies: Durable production data or stateful critical services
notApplies: Reproducible stateless artifacts with no unique data
checks: Map every durable store, object, secret, configuration, and external dependency to backup ownership
Inspect frequency, retention, encryption, immutability, isolation, monitoring, restore order, schema compatibility, and credentials
Compare RPO/RTO targets with tested restore timings and dependencies
manual: Review recent restore evidence and incident communications
Confirm managed-service backup and regional failover settings
safeFixes: Correct runbook steps and add backup monitoring
Add restore validation to an isolated test environment
approval: Deleting backups, changing retention, or initiating production failover
verify: Perform an isolated restore and application integrity check
Record actual recovery point and elapsed time
stack: Restore application, schema, objects, queues, and secrets in dependency order
limitations: A configured backup without a tested restore is NOT_VERIFIED

title: Deployment
purpose: Inspect build promotion, configuration, migrations, rollout, rollback, health, and environment parity.
notApplies: Source-only examples never deployed or distributed
checks: Trace one immutable artifact from source revision through build, test, provenance, promotion, and runtime
Inspect environment validation, secrets, migration ordering, readiness, termination, rollout, rollback, concurrency, and smoke checks
Check preview isolation, production approvals, branch protections, and artifact retention
manual: Review deployed settings and last successful rollback evidence
Confirm operator access and incident procedures
safeFixes: Add preflight validation and post-deploy smoke checks
Pin action versions and clarify rollout documentation
approval: Deploying, rolling back production, changing secrets, or altering production topology
verify: Deploy to an isolated environment and exercise critical checks
Demonstrate rollback or forward-fix with compatible migrations
stack: Use platform-native immutable artifacts and health semantics
limitations: Repository workflows do not prove production settings or permissions

title: Infrastructure
purpose: Audit infrastructure as code, network and identity boundaries, encryption, state, drift, and least privilege.
applies: Cloud, container, orchestration, network, or infrastructure-as-code configuration
notApplies: No managed runtime or infrastructure under project control
checks: Inspect identity, role trust, network exposure, ingress/egress, encryption, keys, secret injection, and metadata access
Review state protection, locking, module versions, destructive changes, drift, tags, quotas, backups, and multi-environment isolation
Run format, validate, lint, policy, and non-mutating plan tools where available
manual: Review live drift, organization policies, and break-glass access
Inspect plan output for replacements and data risk
safeFixes: Pin compatible modules and correct validated non-destructive policy omissions
Add least-privilege documentation and static checks
approval: Applying infrastructure, replacing resources, widening access, or changing production networking
verify: Run validate and policy checks after final edits
Apply only in an authorized isolated environment and inspect resulting controls
stack: Respect provider and IaC tool state, lifecycle, and import semantics
limitations: Static IaC cannot establish live drift or inherited organization policy

title: Software supply chain
purpose: Inspect dependencies, build integrity, provenance, releases, licenses, actions, and secret exposure across the delivery chain.
applies: Any project consuming or publishing software artifacts
notApplies: No exemption for executable release artifacts
checks: Verify lockfile integrity, direct and transitive dependency review, vulnerability output, lifecycle scripts, and abandoned packages
Inspect CI action pinning, token permissions, untrusted build inputs, artifact signing, provenance, checksums, reproducibility, and protected release flow
Validate declared licenses, notices, source attribution, generated-file provenance, and secret scanning
manual: Triage vulnerabilities for actual reachability and compensating controls
Review maintainer and registry trust for critical dependencies
safeFixes: Pin action commits and compatible dependency patches after tests
Correct license inventory and checksums
approval: Major dependency upgrades, replacing registries, rotating tokens, or changing release authority
verify: Rebuild from a clean checkout with the lockfile
Compare artifacts, checksums, SBOM, and provenance
stack: Disable or isolate install scripts where compatible and use least-privilege CI tokens
limitations: A vulnerability identifier alone does not prove exploitability or safety

title: Cost efficiency
purpose: Tie resource and vendor cost to workloads, ownership, unit economics, budgets, and safe optimization choices.
applies: Paid infrastructure, APIs, AI, storage, messaging, or observability
notApplies: No material variable or fixed operating cost
checks: Map cost centers to services, tenants, features, environments, and owners
Inspect idle resources, retention, egress, log cardinality, build minutes, queries, storage lifecycle, and retry amplification
Define budgets, anomaly alerts, unit metrics, and cost-performance-reliability tradeoffs
manual: Review current provider pricing and contractual commitments
Validate product value and growth assumptions
safeFixes: Add cost attribution tags and bounded retention
Remove a proven unused non-production resource through an approved workflow
approval: Deleting resources, changing service tier, retention, reliability, or customer-visible limits
verify: Compare normalized billing before and after over a representative period
Confirm reliability and performance budgets remain satisfied
stack: Include managed-service minimums, egress, support, and observability costs
limitations: Pricing is time-sensitive and must be verified at audit time

title: Documentation
purpose: Verify that user, contributor, architecture, operations, security, and release documentation is accurate and executable.
notApplies: No exemption; scope follows the artifact's audience
checks: Run installation, quick-start, command, configuration, troubleshooting, and contribution steps from a clean context
Check architecture, data, security, deployment, recovery, compatibility, ownership, and release notes against current code
Validate links, examples, diagrams, generated references, accessibility, and secret-free sample values
manual: Review information hierarchy for each audience
Check that limitations and human-only steps are conspicuous
safeFixes: Correct stale commands, links, examples, and diagrams
Add missing evidence-backed operational notes
approval: Changing public commitments, support policy, or legal statements
verify: Follow the quick start in a clean directory
Run link, example, and CLI-help consistency checks
stack: Generate reference material from the same command and schema sources when practical
limitations: Documentation cannot substitute for unimplemented behavior

title: Analytics
purpose: Audit event semantics, consent, data quality, identity, privacy, delivery, and decision usefulness.
applies: Product, marketing, operational, or experimentation analytics
notApplies: No analytics collection or derived behavioral data
checks: Map each event to a decision, owner, schema, trigger, identity, consent state, and retention
Inspect duplicate delivery, ordering, retries, offline queues, bot/internal traffic, versioning, and schema validation
Check personal and sensitive fields, tenant boundaries, deletion propagation, access, and experimentation exposure
manual: Compare sample warehouse events with source actions
Review metric definitions and consent behavior with owners
safeFixes: Remove prohibited fields and add schema validation
Document and de-duplicate a clearly defined event
approval: Adding tracking, changing consent, identity stitching, retention, or metric definitions
verify: Trigger one action and trace its exact event through the pipeline
Test consent denied, offline, retry, and deletion paths
stack: Separate server and client identity sources and avoid embedding secrets
limitations: Warehouse correctness needs sampled destination evidence

title: Notifications
purpose: Inspect email, SMS, push, and in-app notifications for authorization, preferences, retries, privacy, and deliverability.
applies: Transactional, security, lifecycle, or marketing messages
notApplies: No outbound or in-product notification system
checks: Trace trigger, recipient authorization, template data, locale, channel selection, send, webhook, and state update
Inspect idempotency, deduplication, rate limits, quiet hours, retry, expiry, unsubscribe, suppression, and bounce handling
Check sensitive preview content, deep links, spoof resistance, preference overrides, tenant isolation, and provider secrets
manual: Review content accuracy, accessibility, and deliverability settings
Confirm legally required and user-controlled preference semantics
safeFixes: Add deduplication keys, expiry, and sensitive-data redaction
Correct accessible template markup
approval: Changing mandatory-message policy, consent, sender identity, or provider
verify: Send to controlled sinks and trace provider callbacks
Exercise duplicate, stale, opted-out, bounced, and cross-tenant cases
stack: Treat provider webhooks as hostile signed input and make handlers idempotent
limitations: Deliverability and carrier behavior require provider evidence

title: AI-enabled features
purpose: Audit model boundaries, prompt injection, tool authority, data handling, output validation, evaluation, fallback, and cost.
applies: LLM, embedding, classifier, agent, retrieval, or generative-media features
notApplies: No model inference or model-derived decision
checks: Map data, instructions, model, retrieval, tools, outputs, users, and trust boundaries
Inspect prompt injection, instruction/data separation, tool allowlists, per-object authorization, argument validation, confirmation, sandboxing, and output encoding
Review model/version pinning, privacy, retention, training opt-outs, evaluation sets, hallucination handling, moderation, fallback, rate limits, and cost bounds
manual: Adversarially test indirect injection and excessive-agency scenarios
Review high-impact decisions and human oversight
safeFixes: Constrain tool schemas, redact sensitive context, and encode output at its sink
Add deterministic evaluation cases and token limits
approval: Granting new tool authority, changing model provider, sending new sensitive data, or automating high-impact decisions
verify: Run versioned benign, adversarial, multilingual, and failure evaluation sets
Confirm unauthorized tool and data requests are denied at execution time
standards: OWASP LLM Prompt Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
OWASP AI Agent Security Cheat Sheet
stack: Treat model output and retrieved content as untrusted; enforce controls outside the prompt
limitations: Model behavior is probabilistic; report evaluation scope and residual risk

title: Payments
purpose: Audit money movement, pricing, entitlements, provider events, reconciliation, idempotency, and sensitive data boundaries.
applies: Payments, billing, subscriptions, refunds, credits, invoices, or financial ledgers
notApplies: No money, stored value, pricing, or paid entitlement
checks: Trace quote-to-entitlement and refund/dispute flows with currency and minor-unit handling
Inspect server-authoritative amounts, idempotency, webhook raw-body signatures, replay defense, ordering, duplicate events, state machines, and reconciliation
Check authorization, audit trails, secrets, hosted-field boundaries, tax/discount rounding, negative amounts, and failure recovery
manual: Review provider dashboard settings and sample reconciliations
Obtain qualified compliance and financial review where applicable
safeFixes: Add idempotency storage, explicit currency validation, and duplicate-event tests
Redact payment identifiers from logs
approval: Changing financial calculations, prices, ledgers, provider, settlement, or entitlement semantics
verify: Run sandbox success, duplicate, timeout, delayed webhook, refund, and dispute scenarios
Reconcile provider, internal ledger, and granted entitlement
standards: OWASP Third Party Payment Gateway Integration Cheat Sheet
stack: Use provider-hosted collection where possible and never trust client-calculated amounts
limitations: Do not claim PCI or financial compliance from a code audit

title: Realtime communication
purpose: Inspect WebSocket, SSE, subscription, and presence flows for authorization, lifecycle, ordering, abuse, and recovery.
applies: WebSockets, SSE, subscriptions, live presence, or collaborative state
notApplies: Request-response applications with no persistent or pushed channel
checks: Authenticate handshakes and authorize every subscribe, publish, and resource action
Inspect token expiry, revocation, origin, message schema and size, rate limits, backpressure, heartbeats, cleanup, and connection caps
Check ordering, deduplication, cursor/resume, reconnect storms, stale presence, tenant namespaces, and sensitive errors
manual: Observe network interruption and multi-device behavior
Review gateway limits and load-balancer timeouts
safeFixes: Add message bounds, schema validation, and cleanup
Namespace channels and add bounded reconnect jitter
approval: Changing delivery guarantees, channel authorization, or gateway topology
verify: Test expired, revoked, unauthorized, duplicate, out-of-order, and oversized messages
Disconnect abruptly and confirm cleanup and resume semantics
stack: Enforce authorization server-side for each resource, not just at connection time
limitations: Gateway and network behavior require runtime load evidence

title: Offline behavior
purpose: Audit local persistence, queued actions, synchronization, conflicts, revocation, privacy, and recovery under intermittent connectivity.
applies: Offline-capable web, mobile, or desktop applications
Clients that queue writes or cache private state
notApplies: Online-only clients that store no durable application data locally
checks: Inventory locally stored data, cached responses, queued actions, versioning, encryption, and eviction
Inspect duplicate delivery, ordering, conflict detection/resolution, tombstones, schema migration, partial sync, clock skew, and retry bounds
Verify logout, revocation, role/tenant changes, device loss, shared-device privacy, stale authorization, and cache invalidation
manual: Exercise long-offline, low-storage, clock-change, and multi-device edits
Review user-visible conflict and data-loss recovery
safeFixes: Add queue idempotency keys, version markers, and explicit offline states
Clear scoped private caches on verified logout
approval: Changing conflict policy, offline authorization, retention, or destructive synchronization
verify: Run online-offline-reconnect flows with duplicate and conflicting actions
Confirm revoked access does not remain usable offline beyond stated policy
stack: Treat the local database and service-worker cache as separate security boundaries
limitations: Platform background-execution and storage eviction vary by device

title: Orchestrated audit
purpose: Discover the project, select applicable modules, run safe independent checks, merge evidence, and prioritize remediation.
notApplies: A narrowly requested module where orchestration adds no value
checks: Run discovery first and determine applicability from recorded evidence
Execute independent read-only checks concurrently only where safe and preserve raw results
Merge duplicates without losing locations or standards and rank by severity, confidence, impact, and effort
manual: Review applicability decisions and merged-finding fidelity
Approve any risky fix plan before mutation
safeFixes: Apply only fixes each module labels safe when --safe is explicit
Regenerate Markdown and JSON reports
approval: Any risky module change or expansion outside the requested scope
verify: Re-run affected modules and the applicable regression suite
Mark every skipped, blocked, or unverified check explicitly
stack: Use project-native commands discovered from manifests and CI
limitations: Orchestration does not turn unavailable runtime evidence into PASS

title: Release readiness
purpose: Enforce a fail-closed release gate across project checks, findings, generated assets, packages, licenses, and installation.
notApplies: Exploratory work not represented as release-ready
checks: Run applicable format, lint, type, unit, integration, end-to-end, build, security, dependency, migration, authorization, upload, and validation checks
Check canonical/generated synchronization, deterministic packaging, checksums, attribution, and clean installation
Fail for open critical or required high findings, failed gates, incomplete packages, or required high-risk NOT_VERIFIED checks
manual: Review residual risk, skipped checks, release notes, rollback, and human-only publication steps
Confirm production authority before any deployment
safeFixes: No implicit fixes; invoke module fix modes separately with explicit scope
Regenerate deterministic derived assets
approval: Publishing, deploying, bypassing a gate, or accepting high residual risk
verify: Repeat the complete gate after the final change
Install release artifacts in a clean temporary project and invoke the skill
stack: Use the repository's authoritative CI commands and pinned runtime
limitations: A local gate cannot prove remote CI, registry, release, or deployment status
